subtopics.title: Grouped Data Revision — Intervals, Histograms and the Estimated Mean

questions.question: The bars of a histogram touch because:
options: It saves space on the page
The classes are continuous and share boundaries with no gaps
Frequencies are always whole numbers
The data is qualitative

questions.question: For the travel-time data, the modal class is:
options: 10 to 20 minutes
40 to 50 minutes
20 to 30 minutes
0 to 10 minutes

questions.question: The estimated mean of the forty travel times is:
options: 25 minutes
20,50 minutes
23,75 minutes
22,75 minutes

questions.question: The mean of grouped data is only an ESTIMATE because:
options: Each value is assumed to sit at its class midpoint — the raw values are hidden
The calculator rounds each multiplication
Frequencies are approximate counts
The last class is usually open-ended

questions.question: The points of a frequency polygon are plotted at:
options: The upper boundary of each class
The lower boundary of each class
The class midpoints, at the height of each frequency
The cumulative frequencies

questions.question: The polygon is anchored to the horizontal axis by:
options: Plotting zeros at the midpoints of the empty classes before the first and after the last
Drawing vertical lines down from the first and last points
Extending the last line segment to infinity
Shading the area underneath it

questions.question: For the travel-time data, the first two plotted points of the polygon are:
The main advantage of a frequency polygon over a histogram is that it:
options: Shows exact raw data values
Requires no vertical axis
Always looks symmetric
Lets two datasets be compared on the same set of axes

subtopics.title: Ogives — Building the Cumulative Frequency Curve

questions.question: The cumulative frequencies for the travel-time data are:
Each cumulative frequency is plotted at the UPPER class boundary because:
options: The graph looks smoother that way
The midpoint is reserved for the polygon
The running total is only complete at the end of the class
Upper boundaries are easier to read

questions.question: The ogive for this data starts at the point:
An ogive can never slope downward because:
options: The classes are always equal in width
Frequencies are plotted at midpoints
The vertical axis shows percentages
A running total cannot shrink — each class only ever adds to it

subtopics.title: Reading the Ogive — Median, Quartiles and Percentiles

questions.question: For 40 values, the median is read from the ogive at vertical position:
Reading across from 20 and down, the estimated median travel time is about:
options: 20 minutes
30 minutes
23 minutes
16 minutes

questions.question: With Q1 ≈ 14 minutes and Q3 ≈ 30 minutes, the interquartile range is about:
options: 16 minutes
44 minutes
22 minutes
7 minutes

questions.question: To estimate how many learners travel MORE than 35 minutes, you:
options: Read across from 35 on the vertical axis and double the answer
Multiply 35 by the number of classes
Read the frequency of the 30-to-40 class
Go up from 35 to the curve, read the cumulative count, and subtract it from 40

subtopics.title: The Skyline and the Mountain Profile

questions.question: In the skyline picture, each building represents:
options: A class interval, with height showing how many values fall inside
One individual learner
The cumulative total so far
The mean of the dataset

questions.question: The buildings share walls because:
options: The frequencies are equal
Travel time is continuous — 19 and 21 minutes live in neighbouring intervals meeting at 20
The data was collected on the same day
Histograms are always drawn without axes

questions.question: Estimating the mean by placing everyone at their class midpoint is described as:
options: A serious error that should be avoided
Only valid for symmetric data
The fairest guess available once the building has swallowed the detail
The exact mean of the raw data

questions.question: The mountain profile beats the skyline when the task is to:
options: Find the tallest single class
Recover the raw data values
Calculate the total frequency
Compare two datasets on one grid

subtopics.title: The Running Total Tells a Different Story

questions.question: In the stokvel picture, the ogive corresponds to:
options: The list of members' names
The interest earned each month
The total-so-far column of the ledger
The deposit made in a single month

questions.question: The total 16 belongs at 20 minutes on the ogive because:
options: The total is only complete at the end of its class
16 rounded up is 20
20 is the midpoint of the second class
The first class is ignored

questions.question: A steep stretch of the ogive corresponds to:
options: An empty class
A crowded class — the running total grows fast where data is dense
A mistake in the cumulative column
The median of the data

questions.question: If a drawn ogive dips downhill at some point, it means:
options: The data contains negative values
The classes have unequal widths
The dataset is skewed to the left
A subtraction slipped into a column that only ever adds — the graph is wrong

subtopics.title: Across and Down — Reading Answers off the Curve

questions.question: The two-step move for reading a median or quartile off an ogive is:
options: Down from the value, then across to the frequency
Across from the position on the vertical axis to the curve, then down to the value
Up from the midpoint, then across to the cumulative axis
Diagonally from the origin to the curve

questions.question: The 90th percentile of the 40 travel times is read at position:
The interquartile range describes:
options: The span of the middle half of the ordered data
The distance from the minimum to the maximum
The height of the tallest histogram bar
The position of the median

questions.question: Ogive answers should be reported with the word 'approximately' because:
options: The examiner subtracts marks for confidence
Cumulative frequencies are rounded to the nearest ten
The vertical axis has no scale
The raw values are sealed inside classes, so every reading is an estimate
